title: Scalar restriction preserves geometric and open adjunctions
statement: Let $R_n,c_n,B,\psi_n$ be commutative coefficient data satisfying $c_n\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n$, and let $C$ be any exact additive levelwise restriction with identity section and transition identifications as in [lem-sf-semilinear-scalar-restriction]. For the actual varying-ring operations [def-sp-varying-ring-operations] and constant tower operations [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], there are inverse- and direct-image comparison isomorphisms $b_f,d_f$ for every scheme map $f$. The map $d_f$ is identity on the prescribed fibre-product sections. The comparisons preserve the specified unit and counit, and $d_f$ is the mate of $b_f^{-1}$. For every open immersion $j$, there is an extension-by-zero comparison $a_j$ preserving the specified open unit. No coefficient flatness is assumed. The direct-image section normalization is pointwise: for every input section x, its image under d_f is heterogeneously equal to x.

proof.text: At each index n, compose the prescribed level isomorphism for C on Y, the section-normalized moduleEvalP for varying-ring direct image, the existing one-ring scalar/direct-image isomorphism, and the inverse level isomorphism on X. Its section map becomes identity after the prescribed level identifications. The transition equation of C and the product base-change map show that these isomorphisms commute with successor transitions; NatTrans.ofOpSequence assembles them to the natural direct-image isomorphism d. Its pointwise heterogeneous section identity follows from the level-section identities. Use the proved native-carrier evaluation normalization in its separate module, so that continuous-module carrier normalization is not repeated during the assembly. The proved component-transition lemma isolates the successor argument and is applied to this explicitly constructed family.

proof.text: Define b inverse as the inverse adjunction mate of d. The unit normalization of moduleEvalG says that its inverse mates to moduleEvalP. Paste this evaluation square with the proved, invertible, single-ring scalar/pullback square. The mate-of-pasting and mate-of-whiskering identities identify its mate with the evaluated component of d. By the unit characterization of adjoint transposes, the n-th component of b inverse is therefore the composite of the level identifications, the single-ring scalar/pullback isomorphism, and moduleEvalG inverse. All components are invertible, hence so is b inverse. The mate equivalence gives the specified mate equation; the existing scalarMateUnit and scalarMateCounit calculations give unit and counit compatibility.

proof.text: For an open j and an input system M, evaluation identifies the varying-ring extension with the chosen extension at R_n. Combine this isomorphism with C.level. The single-sheaf open-support lemma then shows that the B-open counit at every level of rho_X(extension M) is invertible. Naturality of the counit transports invertibility through these level isomorphisms; termwise evaluation detects invertibility on the strict tower.

proof.text: Take the inverse open mate of b.hom. At M its formula is the B-open extension of rho_U applied to the varying-ring open unit, followed by the B-open extension of b.hom, followed by the B-open counit at rho_X(extension M). The varying-ring open unit is invertible, b is invertible, and the last counit is invertible by the previous step. Thus this mate is invertible and its inverse defines a. The inverse-mate identity and scalarMateUnit give exactly the prescribed open_unit equation. Assemble b,d,a and the section and mate laws into OrdinaryScalarAdjunctions.
